Practice areas

Family

Inheritance and wills
  • Preparing and reviewing a will
  • Declaration of heirs and division of the estate
  • Guidance on inheritance taxes and paperwork
Property and tenancies
  • Drafting and reviewing rental contracts
  • Unpaid rent, deposits and ending a tenancy
  • Home purchases and deposit agreements (arras)
Employment
  • Dismissals and final settlements
  • Claims for unpaid amounts
  • Changes to working conditions
Businesses and self-employed
  • Drafting and reviewing contracts
  • Setting up companies and shareholder agreements
  • Recovering unpaid invoices
Consumer claims
  • Faulty products and services
  • Undue charges and contract terms
  • Prior complaints to the company

    III.

    How we work

    Four clauses. Tap each one for the detail.

    I.First consultation

    We hear your situation, review the documents you bring and explain the options, their time limits and their risks.

    II.Engagement letter

    Before we start, you receive in writing the scope of work, the fees, the likely expenses and the payment terms.

    III.Handling the matter

    We act as agreed and keep you informed of every relevant step in plain language.

    IV.Closing

    We explain the outcome, return your original documents and tell you what to watch afterwards.

    VI.

    Our commitments

    Confidentiality

    What you tell us is protected by professional secrecy.

    Clarity

    We avoid unnecessary jargon and put what matters in writing.

    Honesty

    We do not promise results. No lawyer can guarantee the outcome of a matter.

    Response time

    We reply to your message within two working days (sample timeframe). If you have a deadline, say so when you call.

    VII.

    Frequently asked questions

    What should I bring to the first consultation?

    The documents related to your matter. The tool in clause II gives you an indicative list.

    How much do proceedings cost?

    It depends on the case. We study it first and quote in writing before starting.

    Can the consultation be remote?

    Yes, by video call or phone, as well as at the office.

    I have received a notice. What should I do?

    Contact us as soon as possible and keep the document and the date it arrived. Do not wait for the appointment to tell us there is a deadline.

    Can you assure me it will go well?

    No. No lawyer can guarantee a result. We can explain your options and risks frankly.

    Can I send documents on WhatsApp?

    Not before speaking with the firm. We will give you a suitable way to hand them over.
